newsitem.title: USA: Dow surges to all-time high after tame jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Dow surges to all-time high after tame jobs report.

text.p: Wall Street stocks soared to record highs Thursday after employment and wage data for June offered further evidence that U.S. economic growth remains moderate and inflation remains at bay.
The Dow industrials rose 100 points to close unofficially at 7896, the blue chip average's first new all-time high in nearly two weeks. The broad rally also lifted secondary indexes to record levels.
Stocks surged from the opening bell, rallying in tandem with the bond market on the bullish economic news.
The buying spree was sparked by a surprise uptick in the U.S. unemployment rate to 5.0 percent in June. Economists had predicted the rate would remain at May's 4.8 percent reading.

Also, monthly job growth and hourly wage increases were slightly lower than forecast. Analysts said the data reinforced the idea that economic growth is moderating on its own, confirming the Fed's decision Wednesday to hold interest rates steady and diminishing chances for future increases.
"The economic backdrop at this point appears to be remarkable," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"Inflation is nowhere to be found and investors are beginning to sense the August Fed meeting may also be one where rates are held in check," he said.
Analysts also detected a seasonal note in today's performance by stocks, pointing out that the U.S. Independence Day holiday season has produced more than its share of market fireworks in the past.
"Historically, the stock market usually makes a strong move, in either direction, in the days preceding the Fourth of July," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.
Such was the case a year ago, when a stunningly strong jobs report on the day after the Independence Day holiday initiated a stiff, summer-long stock market correction.

Any fears of a repeat performance dissipated immediately after the June jobs report, which produced a fierce round of buying that continued through the market's early close at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT. U.S. financial markets will remain closed tomorrow for the holiday.
The Dow's rally brought its gain for the holiday-shortened week to 208 points, the best since its record-setting 346.26-point rise in the week ended June 13.
The broad stock market advance saw gaining issues outpace decliners by five to two on volume of more than 370 million shares.

Among individual issues, Northrop Grumman Corp surged 21 points to 109-7/8 after announcing it would merge with aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp in a stock swap valued at about $11.6 billion. Lockheed fell 4-7/8 to 99-1/8.
Pharmaceutical company Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc rose 1-5/8 to 37-5/16 despite announcing that its second quarter earnings would not exceed those of the first quarter.
Investors apparently focused on a restructuring plan unveiled by Pharmacia that the company said would turn its operations around in 1998.

INSO Corp fell 9-11/16 to 11-1/16. Alex. Brown downgraded the shares following INSO's announcement late Wednesday that second quarter results before a planned restructuring charge would fall short of expectations.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 12 points to 1467.61 and the S&P 500 index rose 12.89 points to 916.92, both record highs.
